title: The Workers Letting A.I. Do Their Jobs

sentences.zh: 我凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来一直致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受优惠，请访问 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: For The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittrelle.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的娜塔莉·基特雷尔。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: For the past few years, people all over the world have been asking how AI will change their lives or affect their work.
sentences.zh: 过去几年里，全世界的人们都在问，人工智能将如何改变他们的生活或影响他们的工作。

sentences.en: And the answers range from total salvation to absolute doom.
sentences.zh: 而答案从彻底的救赎到绝对的末日，应有尽有。

sentences.en: At the front lines of all of this are software developers who are using artificial intelligence so much that it's already taking over many of their day-to-day tasks.
sentences.zh: 处于这一切最前沿的是软件开发人员，他们使用人工智能的频率之高，以至于它已经接管了他们许多日常任务。

sentences.en: Today, I talked to Times Magazine writer Clive Thompson about his recent survey of the tech industry to find out what it looks like when people invite AI to do their jobs.
sentences.zh: 今天，我采访了《时代》杂志撰稿人克莱夫·汤普森，谈论了他最近对科技行业的调查，以了解当人们请人工智能来完成工作时，情况会是什么样。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, April 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月14日，星期二。

sentences.en: Clive Thompson, legendary tech reporter, a person whose work I have admired for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 克莱夫·汤普森，传奇科技记者，一位我长期以来一直钦佩其作品的人。

sentences.en: Welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: It's good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So you are here because you've been covering extensively the question of how much AI is affecting the workers who are really the backbone of Silicon Valley, programmers,
sentences.zh: 你今天来是因为你一直在深入报道人工智能对硅谷中坚力量——程序员——的影响程度，

sentences.en: the people who write the code that powers every piece of software we use.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些编写驱动我们所用每一款软件的代码的人们。

sentences.en: This is a group of people you know well, not least of all because you wrote a book about them.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你非常了解的群体，不仅因为你曾为他们写过书。

sentences.en: You spent a lot of time talking to them in recent months.
sentences.zh: 近几个月来，你花了很多时间与他们交谈。

sentences.en: So what did you find?
sentences.zh: 那么你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Walk us through that reporting, what it entailed, and what it unearthed.
sentences.zh: 带我们了解一下你的报道，它包含了什么，又揭示了什么。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: Well, I've been following the arrival or the advent of AI as a tool that can write code for a couple of years now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，几年来我一直关注着人工智能作为一种能编写代码的工具的到来或出现。

sentences.en: But it started to accelerate a lot last year.
sentences.zh: 但去年它开始大幅加速。

sentences.en: And I really just wanted to find out, you know, what was going on in the everyday trenches of software development.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想知道，你知道，软件开发的日常一线到底在发生什么。

sentences.en: So I just hit the road and I talked to about 75 different software developers all around the country.
sentences.zh: 所以我出发去实地考察，采访了全国各地大约75位不同的软件开发人员。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是吗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's a lot.
sentences.zh: 那可不少。

sentences.en: That's a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 确实很多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I might've overdone it, but I really wanted to know what was going on kind of across the board because different software developers have very different types of jobs.
sentences.zh: 我可能做得有点过头了，但我真的很想全面了解情况，因为不同软件开发人员的工作类型差异很大。

sentences.en: So I wanted to talk to people who are doing consulting work for regional banks in Tennessee, people who are doing buzzy little startups,
sentences.zh: 所以我希望能采访到为田纳西州地区银行做咨询工作的人，做热门小初创公司的人，

sentences.en: just the two of them in Silicon Valley trying to, like, make something new.
sentences.zh: 在硅谷只有两个人的团队，试图创造点新东西。

sentences.en: And then, you know, the people that are working at the big software giants like Google and Amazon and Microsoft, where you've got, you know, tens of thousands of developers
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道，在谷歌、亚马逊和微软这样的大型软件巨头工作的人，那里有成千上万的开发人员，

sentences.en: having to take care of these code bases that have been around for 20 years, right?
sentences.zh: 不得不维护这些已经存在了20年的代码库，对吧？

sentences.en: And what do they tell you?
sentences.zh: 他们跟你说了什么？

sentences.en: Well, it was really interesting because what I found was that a lot of the coders, they're writing a lot less code.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很有趣，因为我发现很多程序员写的代码少多了。

sentences.en: Some of them are writing no code at all.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至根本不写代码了。

sentences.en: They are having the AI write it for them.
sentences.zh: 他们让人工智能代劳。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And this transition has happened really quickly.
sentences.zh: 这种转变发生得非常快。

sentences.en: I would say it began heavily in the last six months.
sentences.zh: 我想说它在过去六个月里开始变得剧烈。

sentences.en: It accelerated in the last three months as these AI coding tools have just gotten a lot better.
sentences.zh: 随着这些人工智能编程工具变得越来越好，在过去三个月里它加速了。

sentences.en: And they have started to gain the trust of a lot of programmers, including ones that might've been a little skeptical before.
sentences.zh: 它们已经开始赢得许多程序员的信任，包括那些之前可能还有点怀疑的人。

sentences.en: And it's a really stark change from what things looked like even a year or two ago.
sentences.zh: 这与一两年前的情况相比，是一个非常鲜明的变化。

sentences.en: So you're saying coders aren't coding.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说程序员不再写代码了。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, not all of them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，并非所有人。

sentences.en: It's a gradation.
sentences.zh: 这是一个渐进的过程。

sentences.en: But of the people that I spoke to, a majority of them were outsourcing a lot of their day-to-day programming to AI.
sentences.zh: 但在我采访的人中，大多数人都在将日常编程工作大量外包给人工智能。

sentences.en: There are definitely coders who are writing very little to zero code.
sentences.zh: 确实有程序员写的代码非常少，甚至为零。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's a sea change.
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨变。

sentences.en: It's a big sea change.
sentences.zh: 这是一场巨大的巨变。

sentences.en: And how do they feel about that?
sentences.zh: 他们对此感觉如何？

sentences.en: When I first started the research, I kind of wondered whether some of them were going to be uneasy or unhappy about it, right?
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始研究时，我有点担心他们中是否会有人对此感到不安或不快，对吧？

sentences.en: Because I had known from decades of talking to software developers that they often derived enormous pleasure from writing lines of code.
sentences.zh: 因为我从几十年来与软件开发人员的交谈中得知，他们往往能从编写代码行中获得巨大的快乐。

sentences.en: It was like solving a bunch of little puzzles, and it was just delightful when they did it.
sentences.zh: 这就像解决一堆小谜题，当他们完成时，那种感觉非常美妙。

sentences.en: And so I thought maybe this was going to be deflating or demoralizing, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以我以为这可能会让人感到泄气或沮丧，你知道吗？

sentences.en: But in reality, the great majority of everyone I spoke to was really kind of jazzed and excited
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我采访的大多数人都感到非常兴奋和激动，

sentences.en: about the new powers that the AI was giving them to be able to just say in plain language, here's what I want created.
sentences.zh: 因为人工智能赋予了他们新的能力，让他们能够用简单的语言说出：这是我想要创建的东西。

sentences.en: And then five, 10 minutes later, have the working code back, and they're looking at it.
sentences.zh: 然后五到十分钟后，就能拿到可运行的代码，并进行查看。

sentences.en: What they all said was that they've always loved building things.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，他们一直热爱创造事物。

sentences.en: That's the fun of being a developer is you take an idea you have, and through sweat and work, you turn these magic words into a machine that does things for you.
sentences.zh: 这就是做开发者的乐趣所在，你有一个想法，通过汗水和努力，把这些神奇的词语变成一台为你做事的机器。

sentences.en: And that feels like magic, right?
sentences.zh: 那感觉就像魔法，对吧？

sentences.en: That feels like something from Tolkien.
sentences.zh: 那感觉就像托尔金小说里的东西。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And they still feel that, even though they're not writing as much or any of the code themselves.
sentences.zh: 即使他们自己写的代码变少了，甚至不再写代码，他们依然有那种感觉。

sentences.en: They still feel like they're a sorcerer who's thinking about what needs to be made and then using these tools to bring it into being really quickly.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然觉得自己像个巫师，思考着需要创造什么，然后利用这些工具迅速将其变为现实。

sentences.en: Some of them said they feel that loop of success more quickly because the AI moves faster than they would have done.
sentences.zh: 有些人说他们能更快地感受到那种成功的循环，因为人工智能的运行速度比他们自己做要快得多。

sentences.en: So it was interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣。

sentences.en: A lot of them were really, really pumped, really, really stoked.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人真的非常、非常兴奋，非常、非常激动。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I want to talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈这个。

sentences.en: I want to ask you about this excitement, about this magic that also happens to be this massive disruption in their industry.
sentences.zh: 我想问你关于这种兴奋感，关于这种恰好也是他们行业内巨大颠覆的“魔法”。

sentences.en: But first, I want to just understand how big this shift actually is.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我只想了解这种转变到底有多大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: If you want to understand just how big this change is, you sort of have to understand a bit of the history of software development.
sentences.zh: 如果你想了解这种变化有多大，你必须了解一点软件开发的历史。

sentences.en: So it's been around for maybe 50 or 60 years.
sentences.zh: 它大概存在了五六十年。

sentences.en: It's essentially kind of a new field.
sentences.zh: 本质上这算是一个新兴领域。

sentences.en: Ever since we invented computers, we've been figuring out ways to talk to them,
sentences.zh: 自从我们发明了计算机，我们就一直在寻找与它们对话的方法，

sentences.en: and we've been making those ways to talk to them get a little easier and a little closer to human language.
sentences.zh: 而且我们一直在让这些对话方式变得更容易，更接近人类语言。

sentences.en: So what's happening now with AI is probably the biggest change it's undergone yet.
sentences.zh: 所以现在人工智能发生的事情，可能是它经历过的最大变革。

sentences.en: So in the 1940s, you have the first computer, the ENIAC computer here in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪40年代，美国出现了第一台计算机，ENIAC计算机。

sentences.en: And the way that they programmed it, the programmers, it was a team of women, and they had to literally rewire the entire machine to do something different.
sentences.zh: 当时程序员——那是一个女性团队——编程的方式，是必须逐字逐句地重新连接整台机器才能做不同的事情。

sentences.en: So they're crawling around, sometimes crawling inside the machine and rewiring it to create a new logical system to solve a problem, right?
sentences.zh: 所以她们得爬来爬去，有时甚至爬进机器内部重新接线，以创建一个新的逻辑系统来解决问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: Labor-intensive coding.
sentences.zh: 劳动密集型编程。

sentences.en: Very labor-intensive, yeah.
sentences.zh: 非常劳动密集，是的。

sentences.en: And of course, when computers started to go into industry, it was impractical to require people to crawl around inside them and rewire them for every single new problem.
sentences.zh: 当然，当计算机开始进入工业领域时，要求人们爬进机器内部并为每一个新问题重新接线是不切实际的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So they started making computer languages that you could type these commands, and they would get translated into the instructions that are essentially like digital wiring.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始创建计算机语言，你可以输入这些命令，它们会被翻译成本质上像数字线路一样的指令。

sentences.en: But honestly, the early languages, I mean, I've poked around in them, and I've talked to people that had to write them, and they were really hard.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，早期的语言，我是说，我研究过它们，也和必须编写它们的人谈过，它们真的很难。

sentences.en: Because back in those days, every single little thing in the process of asking a computer to do something, you had to be very specific.
sentences.zh: 因为在那个年代，要求计算机做某事的每一个小步骤，你都必须非常具体。

sentences.en: Like, put this number in your memory here, and then put this other number in your memory here.
sentences.zh: 比如，把这个数字放在内存的这里，然后把另一个数字放在内存的那里。

sentences.en: Now, you're going to add them together and put the sum in here.
sentences.zh: 现在，你要把它们加在一起，把总和放在这里。

sentences.en: And so, it was really like, it was like juggling 900 balls just to get it to the most basic piece of math.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的就像，仅仅为了完成最基本的数学运算，就得像耍900个球一样。

sentences.en: And then over the years, coders said, let's automate some of that labor.
sentences.zh: 后来几年，程序员们说，让我们把部分劳动自动化吧。

sentences.en: Let's make that easier.
sentences.zh: 让我们让它变得更容易。

sentences.en: And they have a funny phrase for it.
sentences.zh: 他们对此有一个有趣的说法。

sentences.en: They call it adding a layer of abstraction.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“增加抽象层”。

sentences.en: So all these little finickety steps that slowed you down a lot in the 60s and 70s, those are kind of gone.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有那些在60和70年代让你慢下来的繁琐步骤，现在基本上都消失了。

sentences.en: Like, I can write code much more quickly.
sentences.zh: 比如，我可以更快地编写代码。

sentences.en: It's much easier to write.
sentences.zh: 编写起来容易多了。

sentences.en: It's kind of more like human language.
sentences.zh: 它更像是人类语言。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Every time they realized that they wanted to accelerate the pace at which they wrote code, they would add another layer of abstraction.
sentences.zh: 每当他们意识到想要加快编写代码的速度时，他们就会增加另一个抽象层。

sentences.en: So, things just kept on getting a little easier every decade.
sentences.zh: 所以，每十年事情都在变得容易一点。

sentences.en: It sounds like what you're describing is a process where you move from actual human beings doing real grunt work to make coding happen,
sentences.zh: 听起来你描述的是一个过程，从人类进行真正的苦力劳动来实现编程，

sentences.en: people putting wires into different slots in computers, to something much more sophisticated over time.
sentences.zh: 人们把电线插进计算机的不同插槽，到随着时间推移变得更加复杂的过程。

sentences.en: But it's still sounding quite tedious.
sentences.zh: 但听起来仍然相当乏味。

sentences.en: Like, you still have to write much of this and deal with your problems, etc.
sentences.zh: 比如，你仍然需要编写大部分代码并处理你的问题等等。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, coding was really a grind.
sentences.zh: 我是说，编程确实是一项苦差事。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, what about now?
sentences.zh: 那么现在呢？

sentences.en: Well, what's happening now is that people are using AI agents to write the code for them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在发生的是人们正在使用人工智能代理来为他们编写代码。

sentences.en: So, they've generally gotten sufficiently trustworthy that a lot of the programmers I was speaking to were just using them to automate a lot of their writing of lines of code.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们通常已经变得足够值得信赖，以至于我采访的许多程序员只是用它们来自动化编写大量的代码行。

sentences.en: So, with AI coding, they will have teams of agents.
sentences.zh: 所以，通过人工智能编程，他们会有代理团队。

sentences.en: Like, you will ask the main agent, hey, write this feature for me.
sentences.zh: 比如，你会问主代理：嘿，帮我写这个功能。

sentences.en: Let's work on a plan.
sentences.zh: 我们来制定一个计划。

sentences.en: The AI will say, here's our plan.
sentences.zh: 人工智能会说：这是我们的计划。

sentences.en: And when I say go, it will spawn other sub-agents to do different parts of the task, right?
sentences.zh: 当我下达指令时，它会生成其他子代理来完成任务的不同部分，对吧？

sentences.en: You'll have one that's writing code and another one that is looking at that code and testing it.
sentences.zh: 你会有一个负责写代码的，另一个负责查看代码并进行测试。

sentences.en: And if there are errors, and, you know, there's almost always errors the first time, another agent will look at those error messages and go,
sentences.zh: 如果有错误——你知道，第一次几乎总是会有错误——另一个代理会查看那些错误信息并说：

sentences.en: oh, okay, let's change the code and test it again and keep on going in this little loop, like a little team of agents all working in a swarm.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的，让我们修改代码并再次测试，然后继续在这个小循环中进行，就像一个小代理团队在蜂群中工作一样。

sentences.en: And only at the point in time where they're like, okay, it's passing its test, it's not producing any errors, then it'll go back to the human and say,
sentences.zh: 只有当它们觉得：好的，它通过了测试，没有产生任何错误，那时它才会回到人类面前说：

sentences.en: okay, here's the code, here's the test we wrote, here's the results, you can see our work.
sentences.zh: 好的，这是代码，这是我们写的测试，这是结果，你可以看到我们的工作。

sentences.en: And that's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: There's really very few people having experiences like that other than computer programmers right now.
sentences.zh: 目前除了计算机程序员之外，真的很少有人有这样的体验。

sentences.en: So, what you're describing sounds like an enormous leap from the progress that we've seen over the course of time in coding.
sentences.zh: 所以，你所描述的听起来像是我们在编程史上所见进步的巨大飞跃。

sentences.en: How is it changing things practically for coders?
sentences.zh: 这对程序员来说，在实践中是如何改变事情的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, it's making it a lot quicker to do a lot of things, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，它让做很多事情变得快多了，对吧？

sentences.en: A lot of software developers will tell me that it's just dramatically accelerating the pace at which they work.
sentences.zh: 很多软件开发人员会告诉我，它极大地加快了他们的工作节奏。

sentences.en: And to give you a sense of just how fast it can be, if you're like a small startup, these two-person shops, and I visited some of them,
sentences.zh: 为了让你感受一下它到底有多快，如果你是一家小型初创公司，这种两人团队的店铺，我参观过一些，

sentences.en: they would tell me that they were moving up to 20 times faster than they would have if they were trying to build that company two years ago, right?
sentences.zh: 他们会告诉我，他们的速度比两年前试图建立那家公司时快了20倍，对吧？

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's crazy.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: As some of them said to me, you know, a request from a customer for a new feature that might have taken like a full day could be done in maybe half an hour.
sentences.zh: 正如其中一些人对我说的，你知道，客户提出的一个可能需要整整一天才能完成的新功能需求，现在可能半小时就能搞定。

sentences.en: That's wild.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: 20 minutes to write it, 10 minutes just to look it over it and make sure it's good, right?
sentences.zh: 20分钟写出来，10分钟检查一下确保没问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Now, I should say that this is true of a smaller company where you're kind of writing entirely new code and you don't have to worry about breaking something that already exists.
sentences.zh: 当然，我得说这适用于那种规模较小的公司，你基本上是在写全新的代码，不必担心破坏现有的东西。

sentences.en: So, when you go to really big mature companies, they're using AI, but their metabolism is a lot slower.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你去那些真正大型、成熟的公司时，他们也在用AI，但他们的代谢速度要慢得多。

sentences.en: They're being more cautious.
sentences.zh: 他们会更谨慎。

sentences.en: And so, when I went to Google, they were saying like, at a small startup, you know, 100% of the lines of code are written by AI.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我去了谷歌，他们说，在一家小型初创公司，你知道，100%的代码行都是由AI编写的。

sentences.en: At Google, it's more like maybe 40 or 50%.
sentences.zh: 而在谷歌，这个比例可能只有40%或50%。

sentences.en: And it has sped up their overall metabolism by really only like 10%.
sentences.zh: 而且AI实际上只让他们的整体代谢速度加快了大约10%。

sentences.en: Although, as the developers at Google told me, like, hey, 10% for a company our size, that's a huge win.
sentences.zh: 尽管正如谷歌的开发人员告诉我的那样，嘿，对于我们这种规模的公司来说，10%的提升已经是一个巨大的胜利了。

sentences.en: So, the AI is making them faster at coding, in some cases doing a lot of that work for them.
sentences.zh: 所以，AI确实让他们编码更快了，在某些情况下，AI甚至替他们完成了大量工作。

sentences.en: But it sounds like they still have their jobs.
sentences.zh: 但听起来他们还是保住了自己的工作。

sentences.en: So, for the coders who aren't doing coding anymore, what do their jobs actually look like now?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那些不再亲自写代码的程序员来说，他们现在的工作到底是什么样的呢？

sentences.en: Well, their job, in a way, is to think about what the software ought to be doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在某种程度上，他们的工作是思考软件应该实现什么功能。

sentences.en: Now, that was always their job, right?
sentences.zh: 这本来一直就是他们的工作，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, they always had to think about the shape of the software and then slowly, painstakingly make it happen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们一直都需要构思软件的形态，然后缓慢而费力地将其实现。

sentences.en: And because they don't have to spend so much time on the slow, painstaking, they can spend more time experimentally iterating, right?
sentences.zh: 正因为他们不必再花那么多时间在缓慢、费力的工作上，他们可以花更多时间进行实验性迭代，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I talked to a lot of developers who would say, now that I'm talking to the AI and it's doing the coding,
sentences.zh: 比如，我和许多开发人员聊过，他们会说，既然我在和AI对话，而AI在负责编码，

sentences.en: we'll run through like 10 different possibilities and I'll pick the absolute best one.
sentences.zh: 我们就可以尝试10种不同的可能性，然后我选出绝对最好的一种。

sentences.en: They said, it feels like being Steve Jobs, where you'd go to their minions, bring me nine designs of the iPod and I will handle them each and pick the best one, right?
sentences.zh: 他们说，这感觉就像成了史蒂夫·乔布斯，你会对下属说，给我拿来九个iPod的设计方案，我会一一过目并选出最好的一个，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Several of them literally said the Steve Jobs comparison.
sentences.zh: 他们中有好几个人都亲口用了史蒂夫·乔布斯这个比喻。

sentences.en: So, they're kind of becoming less like construction workers and more like architects.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们变得越来越不像建筑工人，而更像是建筑师了。

sentences.en: But on a deeper level, what they're really doing is just talking.
sentences.zh: 但从更深层次来看，他们真正做的事情其实就是交流。

sentences.en: They're having a lot of conversations.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了大量的对话。

sentences.en: With AI.
sentences.zh: 与AI对话。

sentences.en: Yes, with AI.
sentences.zh: 是的，与AI对话。

sentences.en: They're having conversations with AI and having to be very clear.
sentences.zh: 他们正在与AI进行对话，并且必须表达得非常清晰。

sentences.en: The thing about AI is like, it will go off and do the wrong thing if you're not incredibly clear.
sentences.zh: AI的问题在于，如果你表达得不够极其清晰，它就会跑偏，做错事情。

sentences.en: And how did they find the process of communicating all day long?
sentences.zh: 那么他们觉得整天进行沟通的过程如何呢？

sentences.en: Are they good at it?
sentences.zh: 他们擅长吗？

sentences.en: Do they have to develop that skill?
sentences.zh: 他们必须培养这种技能吗？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I had some of them say that they were surprised to find that they were becoming better communicators.
sentences.zh: 我有一些受访者说，他们惊讶地发现自己正在成为更好的沟通者。

sentences.en: Like, better communicators in English, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，英语表达能力更好了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, they're writing emails better.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们写邮件写得更好了。

sentences.en: The fact that they've had to become better communicators to the AI has made them better communicators to the world in general.
sentences.zh: 为了与AI沟通而不得不成为更好的沟通者，这一事实使他们成为了与现实世界沟通时更好的沟通者。

sentences.en: The bot has made them better at communicating, at having human relationships, potentially?
sentences.zh: 机器人让他们变得更善于沟通，甚至可能更善于处理人际关系了？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know if human relationships would be the way, although...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道人际关系是否是这样，尽管……

sentences.en: That's a bridge too far.
sentences.zh: 那有点扯远了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Well, although there is one coder, Manu Ebert.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过有一位程序员，Manu Ebert。

sentences.en: He's a software developer with a small new startup, a company called Hyperspell.
sentences.zh: 他是一家名为Hyperspell的小型初创公司的软件开发人员。

sentences.en: He sort of said, you know, kind of jokingly, but he said it, like, I wonder if we're finally teaching all the nerds empathy.
sentences.zh: 他半开玩笑地说，但他确实说了，我想知道我们是否终于在教所有的书呆子们什么是同理心了。

sentences.en: Because, you know, they're having to do...
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，他们不得不去做……

sentences.en: Nerds have empathy.
sentences.zh: 书呆子也有同理心。

sentences.en: I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: Nerds have empathy.
sentences.zh: 书呆子也有同理心。

sentences.en: I'm a nerd.
sentences.zh: 我就是个书呆子。

sentences.en: I have empathy.
sentences.zh: 我有同理心。

sentences.en: His point was, you know, I think, correct, that the job didn't used to require quite so much communication, and now it does.
sentences.zh: 他的观点是，我认为是正确的，即这份工作过去并不需要那么多的沟通，但现在需要了。

sentences.en: Talk to me about how Manu's work is changing.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊Manu的工作是如何改变的吧。

sentences.en: He's interesting.
sentences.zh: 他很有意思。

sentences.en: So, Manu has been a developer for a long time, and he's worked at very large companies.
sentences.zh: Manu做开发人员已经很久了，他在非常大的公司工作过。

sentences.en: He's done his own startups.
sentences.zh: 他也做过自己的初创公司。

sentences.en: And when he first started using AI, he wasn't really sure about it.
sentences.zh: 当他刚开始使用AI时，他其实并不确定。

sentences.en: He was worried that it was going to hallucinate things, that it would produce code that would be too flabby or inefficient.
sentences.zh: 他担心AI会产生幻觉，担心它写出的代码会过于臃肿或低效。

sentences.en: And what he said is that over the months, his concerns began to boil away.
sentences.zh: 而他说，几个月下来，他的担忧开始烟消云散了。

sentences.en: He got more confident when he could see that it could do things reliably.
sentences.zh: 当他看到AI能可靠地完成任务时，他变得更有信心了。

sentences.en: So, Manu does something that I actually heard several developers have settled on as an interesting technique,
sentences.zh: 所以，Manu做了一件事，我听说很多开发人员都将其作为一种有趣的技巧，

sentences.en: which is when they want to write a new feature or write a new function or improve some aspect of code,
sentences.zh: 那就是当他们想编写一个新功能、写一个新函数或改进代码的某个方面时，

sentences.en: they will essentially get into a conversation, like a Socratic dialogue with their agent.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上会进入一种对话，就像与他们的代理进行苏格拉底式的对话一样。

sentences.en: They'll say, okay, ask me questions about how this software feature should work.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，好吧，问我关于这个软件功能应该如何工作的问题。

sentences.en: And the agent's like, okay, what is this going to do?
sentences.zh: 然后代理会说，好的，这个功能要做什么？

sentences.en: Should it do it this way?
sentences.zh: 应该这样做吗？

sentences.en: Is it going to be written in this language or in this language?
sentences.zh: 是用这种语言写还是用那种语言写？

sentences.en: By having it interview the coder, as it were, it got them to think about what the software should really be doing.
sentences.zh: 通过让AI采访程序员，它促使他们思考软件真正应该做什么。

sentences.en: And then it was off to the races with having the AI agent do things.
sentences.zh: 然后，让AI代理去执行任务就顺理成章了。

sentences.en: The problem is that I don't mean to anthropomorphize it, but it can sort of misbehave.
sentences.zh: 问题是，我不是要将它拟人化，但它确实会表现得有些不听话。

sentences.en: Manu would tell me there are times when the AI would go off and come back and say, oh, well, I didn't do those tests.
sentences.zh: Manu告诉我，有时AI会跑去执行任务，回来后说，哦，我没做那些测试。

sentences.en: I didn't think they were that important.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们没那么重要。

sentences.en: And he's like, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 然后他就会说，等一下。

sentences.en: Those tests are completely important, you know.
sentences.zh: 那些测试非常重要，你知道的。

sentences.en: And so he would have to figure out ways to sort of reprimand it or ways to cajole or punish it in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须想办法去训斥它，或者想办法哄骗它，或者以某种方式惩罚它。

sentences.en: How do you punish AI?
sentences.zh: 你怎么惩罚AI？

sentences.en: Well, you yell at it, basically.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上就是对它大吼大叫。

sentences.en: What Manu would do is he would write these very stern list of instructions, like 10 commandments.
sentences.zh: Manu的做法是写下一份非常严厉的指令清单，就像十诫一样。

sentences.en: And he would have this file.
sentences.zh: 他会有这样一个文件。

sentences.en: He would say, every time you do anything, you look at this file first and you always follow these commandments.
sentences.zh: 他会说，每次你做任何事情，先看这个文件，并且必须始终遵守这些诫命。

sentences.en: Very stern commands, like you must test the code in this way or that.
sentences.zh: 非常严厉的命令，比如你必须以这种或那种方式测试代码。

sentences.en: You must do these things.
sentences.zh: 你必须做这些事情。

sentences.en: You must not do that.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不能做那个。

sentences.en: And software developers, they would show me these commandments and they would be an uppercase, like they're yelling at it.
sentences.zh: 软件开发人员会向我展示这些诫命，它们都是大写的，就像在对它大吼大叫一样。

sentences.en: And they would repeat things over and over again, like they were trying to hypnotize the AI agent by sheer repetition.
sentences.zh: 他们会一遍又一遍地重复同样的事情，就像试图通过纯粹的重复来催眠AI代理一样。

sentences.en: Or they would say things like, if you don't do these tests, I will be fired.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会说，如果你不做这些测试，我会被解雇的。

sentences.en: They would have this very...
sentences.zh: 他们会用这种非常……

sentences.en: Wow, really raising the stakes.
sentences.zh: 哇，真的把赌注提高了。

sentences.en: In very emotional language.
sentences.zh: 用非常情绪化的语言。

sentences.en: One of Manu Ebert's prompts would say that failure to do these tests is unacceptable and embarrassing.
sentences.zh: Manu Ebert的一条提示词会说，不执行这些测试是不可接受且令人尴尬的。

sentences.en: Embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 令人尴尬。

sentences.en: Embarrassing, yeah.
sentences.zh: 令人尴尬，是的。

sentences.en: I asked him, I said, does that work?
sentences.zh: 我问他，我说，这管用吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，管用。

sentences.en: I was going to ask, aren't we supposed to be being nice to these AIs just in case the robots end up taking over the world?
sentences.zh: 我正想问，我们不是应该对这些AI好一点吗，万一机器人最终接管了世界呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, don't eat me.
sentences.zh: 是的，别吃我。

sentences.en: I mean, in one sense, I understood why it works.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种意义上说，我理解为什么它管用。

sentences.en: It's because large language models, I mean, they're language machines.
sentences.zh: 因为大语言模型，我的意思是，它们是语言机器。

sentences.en: And so they understand the meaning of language based on the company it keeps.
sentences.zh: 所以它们根据语言所处的语境来理解语言的含义。

sentences.en: So if they see the word embarrassing, they understand that like, oh, that word, that comes from a bad neighborhood, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果它们看到“尴尬”这个词，它们就会明白，哦，那个词，它来自一个不好的语境，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, there's bad things there and there's embarrassing humiliation, you know, whatnot.
sentences.zh: 就像，那里有不好的事情，有尴尬的羞辱，你知道，诸如此类的。

sentences.en: And so that just helps raise the stakes so that it grasps the import of those words.
sentences.zh: 所以这有助于提高赌注，让它理解这些词的重要性。

sentences.en: So it turns out that actually emotional language and stern and even harsh language probably does have an effect, right?
sentences.zh: 所以事实证明，情绪化的语言，甚至是严厉甚至苛刻的语言，可能确实有效果，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it seems kind of nuts on the surface.
sentences.zh: 表面上看这似乎有点疯狂。

sentences.en: But when you think about the way large language models work, it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 但当你考虑到大语言模型的工作方式时，这就说得通了。

sentences.en: Okay, you have done a very good job of describing why coders like this new way of working.
sentences.zh: 好的，你已经非常出色地描述了为什么程序员喜欢这种新的工作方式。

sentences.en: From what you said, it seems pretty obvious that there are many upsides of this for the people doing this work.
sentences.zh: 从你所说的来看，对于从事这项工作的人来说，这显然有很多好处。

sentences.en: It sounds like they just feel much more powerful overall.
sentences.zh: 听起来他们整体上感觉强大多了。

sentences.en: Yeah, most of the coders I spoke to were just sort of astonished at how much more productive they felt.
sentences.zh: 是的，我采访的大多数程序员都对他们感觉自己效率提高了多少感到惊讶。

sentences.en: They would say things like, you know, I've had this to-do list of things haunting me for years and I'm knocking it all off.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，你知道，我有一个困扰我多年的待办事项清单，现在我正在把它们全部搞定。

sentences.en: I'm getting it done.
sentences.zh: 我正在完成它们。

sentences.en: So overall, there is a real sense of excitement, even giddiness at times.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，有一种真正的兴奋感，有时甚至是眩晕感。

sentences.en: But there are some concerns.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些担忧。

sentences.en: They're worried about losing their skills if they rely too much on AI.
sentences.zh: 他们担心如果过度依赖AI，会丧失自己的技能。

sentences.en: They're worried about jobs being taken away by AI.
sentences.zh: 他们担心工作会被AI取代。

sentences.en: And they worry that they're moving too quickly.
sentences.zh: 而且他们担心自己前进得太快了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是Winnalou。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Okay, Clive, I want to talk about those fears.
sentences.zh: 好的，Clive，我想谈谈那些恐惧。

sentences.en: Can we dig into them?
sentences.zh: 我们可以深入探讨一下吗？

sentences.en: Are they right to be worried about the things that you laid out?
sentences.zh: 他们担心你列出的那些事情是对的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: The concern about de-skilling is really interesting because a lot of the people that I was talking to for this story were, they're a little more senior.
sentences.zh: 关于技能退化的担忧非常有趣，因为我为这个故事采访的很多人，他们资历都比较深。

sentences.en: So they're the generation that knows code really well because they still had to do it by hand.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是那一代人，他们非常了解代码，因为他们仍然必须亲手编写代码。

sentences.en: And so they would tell me that it's great for us to have the AI agents because if they produce
sentences.zh: 所以他们会告诉我，拥有AI代理对我们来说很棒，因为如果它们产生

sentences.en: something wrong or flabby, we have the experience to look at that and go, that's not good.
sentences.zh: 了错误或臃肿的东西，我们有经验去审视它并说，这不好。

sentences.en: Do it again.
sentences.zh: 重做一遍。

sentences.en: And they would all say, well, you know, what about the next generation?
sentences.zh: 他们都会说，嗯，你知道，下一代怎么办？

sentences.en: Are we going to discover five or 10 years now that the next generation of software developers,
sentences.zh: 我们会在五到十年后发现下一代软件开发人员，

sentences.en: you know, simply don't have that deep code sense that lets them be really, really good engineers?
sentences.zh: 你知道，根本没有那种让他们成为真正优秀的工程师的深厚代码感吗？

sentences.en: And a related concern there is that because they're not writing code so much anymore or at all in some cases, they worry that they're losing a bit of that code sense, right?
sentences.zh: 还有一个相关的担忧是，因为他们不再那么频繁地编写代码，或者在某些情况下根本不写了，他们担心自己正在失去一点那种代码感，对吧？

sentences.en: If you don't use it, you're going to lose it.
sentences.zh: 如果你不用它，你就会失去它。

sentences.en: One person I talked to who was worried about the way AI coding tools were de-skilling her was Pia Torian.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的一个担心AI编码工具导致她技能退化的人是Pia Torian。

sentences.en: She was a reasonably newer developer.
sentences.zh: 她是一位相对较新的开发人员。

sentences.en: And so she was in some of her early jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以她正处于职业生涯的早期。

sentences.en: Her employers were like, we want you to use Copilot by Microsoft to write code.
sentences.zh: 她的雇主说，我们希望你使用微软的Copilot来编写代码。

sentences.en: And she was doing hundreds of prompts a day for months.
sentences.zh: 她连续几个月每天都要进行数百次提示。

sentences.en: And she started feeling, wow, this is actually degrading my own knowledge of code.
sentences.zh: 她开始感到，哇，这实际上正在削弱我自己的代码知识。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm losing my ability to code.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我正在失去编码的能力。

sentences.en: That's what she told me.
sentences.zh: 这就是她告诉我的。

sentences.en: Okay, that sounds unsettling for her.
sentences.zh: 好的，这对她来说听起来很令人不安。

sentences.en: But why is it a problem that she's losing her coding skills if AI can do that for her?
sentences.zh: 但如果人工智能可以代劳，她失去编程技能又有什么问题呢？

sentences.en: I don't know how to typeset.
sentences.zh: 我不会排版。

sentences.en: I don't do calligraphy, right?
sentences.zh: 我也不做书法，对吧？

sentences.en: It's never been an issue for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说从来都不是问题。

sentences.en: Aren't there certain things that we can just say, okay, we've moved past this as a society?
sentences.zh: 难道有些事情我们不能直接说，好吧，作为一个社会，我们已经跨越了这个阶段了吗？

sentences.en: Is this one of those things?
sentences.zh: 这是其中之一吗？

sentences.en: Well, this is the great debate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是伟大的辩论所在。

sentences.en: And I don't have an answer for that.
sentences.zh: 我对此也没有答案。

sentences.en: I can tell you that there are two camps of this in the world of software.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你，在软件领域对此有两大阵营。

sentences.en: And they are heatedly opposed to each other.
sentences.zh: 而且他们激烈地对立着。

sentences.en: There is what I would say is probably the majority of the developers who are a little less worried about that.
sentences.zh: 可以说，大多数开发人员对这一点不太担心。

sentences.en: They think that the AI is good enough and will continue to be good enough that it will actually
sentences.zh: 他们认为人工智能已经足够好，并且会持续保持足够好的水平，以至于它实际上

sentences.en: be better at doing a lot of this code than the humans are because it won't make the stupid human mistakes.
sentences.zh: 在处理许多代码方面会比人类更好，因为它不会犯那些愚蠢的人类错误。

sentences.en: You know, people think of code as like this magical thing where you have to work really hard at it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们认为代码是一种神奇的东西，你必须非常努力地去钻研它。

sentences.en: But a lot of it is just doing the same thing over and over and over again, right?
sentences.zh: 但其中很多工作只是在不断地重复做同样的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Extremely rote, tedious work.
sentences.zh: 极其机械、乏味的工作。

sentences.en: It's rote and tedious.
sentences.zh: 既机械又乏味。

sentences.en: And when humans do it, we make mistakes and the robots don't, right?
sentences.zh: 当人类做这些工作时，我们会犯错，而机器人不会，对吧？

sentences.en: So you could make an argument, and this cohort of developers do, that the software will actually be more reliable because the agents are doing all of it.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以提出一个论点，这群开发人员也确实这么认为，即软件实际上会更可靠，因为所有工作都由智能体来完成。

sentences.en: But then there's a very strong argument by a smaller cohort that say, no, when you write new code, it's not just something you build and it stays up.
sentences.zh: 但随后，一小部分人提出了一个非常有力的论点，他们说，不，当你编写新代码时，它不仅仅是你构建完就能一直运行的东西。

sentences.en: You have to maintain it.
sentences.zh: 你必须维护它。

sentences.en: As you add new things to it, adjacent to it that interact with it, there might be interactions that are bad or weird.
sentences.zh: 当你向它添加与之交互的新内容时，可能会产生糟糕或奇怪的交互。

sentences.en: And so the code that the AI is writing might look good right now, but there's a potential that down the line, it could cause really difficult or nasty interactions with other
sentences.zh: 所以人工智能编写的代码现在看起来可能不错，但未来有可能导致与其他

sentences.en: parts of the code base.
sentences.zh: 代码库部分产生非常困难或棘手的交互。

sentences.en: There could be subtle bugs that we don't see right now that really start to pile up in five years now, you've got a huge mess.
sentences.zh: 可能会有一些我们现在看不到的细微漏洞，五年后开始堆积起来，你就面临一个巨大的烂摊子。

sentences.en: So there's a cohort of coders that are saying, we shouldn't be using this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以有一群程序员说，我们不应该使用这些东西。

sentences.en: Not at scale, not the way they're using it right now.
sentences.zh: 不能大规模使用，不能像他们现在这样使用。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I want to return to the question of job loss, which was another fear that you mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我想回到失业这个问题上，这是你提到的另一个担忧。

sentences.en: Do you think that all of this means that junior coders right now are actually somewhat replaceable
sentences.zh: 你认为这一切是否意味着初级程序员现在实际上在某种程度上是可以被取代的

sentences.en: in this field and that maybe in the near future, there will be no such thing as a junior coder
sentences.zh: 在这个领域，也许在不久的将来，根本就不会有初级程序员这种职位了

sentences.en: at all because that entire job category will disappear in the same way that the job of typesetter did?
sentences.zh: 因为整个工作类别会像排版员的工作一样消失？

sentences.en: I think there's definitely a danger that the demand for new junior hires is going to soften.
sentences.zh: 我认为对新初级员工的需求将会疲软，这绝对是一种危险。

sentences.en: And I think we've already seen that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们已经看到了这一点。

sentences.en: You know, if you look at the research of Eric Benjolson at Stanford, he analyzed job postings, job hirings, and he found that in software developers, it was down by 16%, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你看看斯坦福大学埃里克·布林约尔松（Eric Brynjolfsson）的研究，他分析了职位发布和招聘情况，发现软件开发人员的招聘需求下降了16%，对吧？

sentences.en: And that was already happening just in the last, you know, year or so.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是在过去一年左右的时间里就已经发生的了。

sentences.en: So if that's happening when the AI coding tools are really just going from a crawl to a walk to a run, what might happen when they're sprinting?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果人工智能编程工具仅仅是从爬行到行走再到奔跑的过程中就发生了这种情况，那么当它们开始冲刺时会发生什么？

sentences.en: And the other problem, of course, is, you know, this is capitalism, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，另一个问题是，你知道，这是资本主义，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, all of these large firms are always looking for ways to save money.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些大公司都在寻找省钱的方法。

sentences.en: And at high-tech companies, some of the most expensive money are the salaries of these developers, you know?
sentences.zh: 在高科技公司，最昂贵的开支之一就是这些开发人员的薪水，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So the idea of like, oh, we can replace even a chunk of them with AI, that's really compelling.
sentences.zh: 所以，哦，我们可以用人工智能取代他们中的一部分，这个想法真的很有吸引力。

sentences.en: And we're seeing this across all forms of white-collar labor right now, right?
sentences.zh: 我们现在在所有形式的白领劳动中都看到了这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: All the C-suite folks love the idea of being able to either lay people off because they can replace them with AI or threaten to do so, right?
sentences.zh: 所有高管都喜欢这种想法，要么因为可以用人工智能取代员工而裁员，要么威胁要这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: Because even if you're not replaced by AI, if you de-skill and devalue the job, it just gets easier for the owners to push you around.
sentences.zh: 因为即使你没有被人工智能取代，如果你失去了技能，工作价值被贬低，老板就更容易摆布你了。

sentences.en: Clive, if coding is at the vanguard of AI affecting work, the amount of it, the quality of it, what does all of this mean for the rest of us who don't work as coders?
sentences.zh: 克莱夫，如果编程是人工智能影响工作的先锋，无论是工作量还是质量，这对我们这些不从事编程工作的人来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: Will white-collar or blue-collar workers in other fields see AI take over in a similar way?
sentences.zh: 其他领域的白领或蓝领工人会看到人工智能以类似的方式接管工作吗？

sentences.en: What developers are experiencing right now is something that maybe seems a little paradoxical, which is that they had spent years developing these very, very hard technical skills.
sentences.zh: 开发人员现在所经历的事情似乎有点矛盾，那就是他们花了多年时间培养这些非常、非常硬核的技术技能。

sentences.en: And it turns out those are some of the easiest things to automate, right?
sentences.zh: 结果发现这些技能反而是最容易自动化的，对吧？

sentences.en: The hard stuff to automate is like talking to our colleagues and our customers and figuring out what should we be building, right?
sentences.zh: 难以自动化的东西是与同事和客户沟通，弄清楚我们应该构建什么，对吧？

sentences.en: Setting priorities, setting strategy.
sentences.zh: 设定优先级，制定战略。

sentences.en: AI can't do that, right?
sentences.zh: 人工智能做不到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: There are still truly human skills.
sentences.zh: 这些仍然是真正的人类技能。

sentences.en: There are still truly human skills.
sentences.zh: 这些仍然是真正的人类技能。

sentences.en: And so I began to wonder if that's a pattern we might see in other forms of white-collar work.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始怀疑这是否是我们可能在其他形式的白领工作中看到的模式。

sentences.en: Like back in the 80s, it seemed like chess was so hard to play, there was no way a computer was going to do it.
sentences.zh: 就像在80年代，下棋似乎很难，计算机根本不可能做到。

sentences.en: But it seemed like speaking, that's easy.
sentences.zh: 但说话似乎很容易。

sentences.en: Surely a computer should be able to just speak.
sentences.zh: 计算机肯定应该能够直接说话。

sentences.en: But it turned out that chess was actually easier for computers to do than to learn to speak.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，对计算机来说，下棋实际上比学习说话更容易。

sentences.en: They conquered chess in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 它们在90年代就征服了国际象棋。

sentences.en: And it took like two decades more to learn how to talk like a human.
sentences.zh: 而学习像人类一样说话又多花了大约二十年时间。

sentences.en: So one of the things I think we see with AI is that things that we thought maybe were like, oh, this is my big skill.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们在人工智能身上看到的一件事是，那些我们认为，哦，这是我的核心技能的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's not really your skill.
sentences.zh: 是的，那其实并不是你的技能。

sentences.en: Your skill lies elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 你的技能在于其他方面。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So the process that you're talking about is essentially one in which in different fields, we kind of learn the thing that is not automatable, that a bot can't do.
sentences.zh: 所以你谈论的过程本质上是，在不同的领域，我们学会了什么是不可自动化的，什么是机器人做不到的。

sentences.en: And where people sort of focus on that.
sentences.zh: 人们开始关注这一点。

sentences.en: How long do you think it's going to take for those transformations to hit jobs en masse?
sentences.zh: 你认为这些转变大规模影响工作需要多长时间？

sentences.en: My crystal ball was that it's going to be longer than we think for the following reason.
sentences.zh: 我的水晶球显示，由于以下原因，这需要的时间比我们想象的要长。

sentences.en: What we learned from the history of computers is that it can take things a lot longer to have an impact on corporate life than we would expect.
sentences.zh: 我们从计算机历史中学到的是，事物对企业生活产生影响所需的时间可能比我们预期的要长得多。

sentences.en: So back in the 80s and early 90s, you get the advent of the personal computer.
sentences.zh: 回到80年代和90年代初，个人电脑出现了。

sentences.en: A company can now, instead of having someone type memos on a typewriter, they can do it on a computer.
sentences.zh: 公司现在不需要有人用打字机打备忘录，他们可以在电脑上完成。

sentences.en: And there's this assumption that it's going to dramatically increase the productivity of companies.
sentences.zh: 人们假设这会极大地提高公司的生产力。

sentences.en: And at first, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但起初并没有。

sentences.en: And economists are kind of baffled by this.
sentences.zh: 经济学家对此感到困惑。

sentences.en: And it was because to actually increase productivity or efficiency of companies, the company had to reorganize the way it did business around the computers, right?
sentences.zh: 这是因为要真正提高公司的生产力或效率，公司必须围绕计算机重新组织其业务方式，对吧？

sentences.en: They had to start going, well, we don't need you to just treat the computer like a typewriter and print up a memo and then send it to everyone.
sentences.zh: 他们必须开始意识到，好吧，我们不需要你把电脑当作打字机，打印出一份备忘录然后发给每个人。

sentences.en: Just email it to someone.
sentences.zh: 直接发电子邮件给某人就行了。

sentences.en: That means everyone at all our regional offices can all be reading the same stuff at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们所有区域办事处的每个人都可以同时阅读相同的内容。

sentences.en: And so once they began to reorganize the way that information and decisions flowed around
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦他们开始围绕计算机和互联网的便利性重新组织信息和决策的流动方式，

sentences.en: the affordances of computers and the internet, then you began to see changes in efficiency, productivity, and GDP.
sentences.zh: 你就会开始看到效率、生产力和GDP的变化。

sentences.en: But it took a long time.
sentences.zh: 但这花了很多时间。

sentences.en: And my suspicion would be that it's going to be the same way with AI.
sentences.zh: 我的怀疑是，人工智能也会经历同样的过程。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: I want to ask about that because it feels to me as though everything has been on a really
sentences.zh: 我想问一下这个问题，因为我觉得最近一切似乎都处于一个非常

sentences.en: accelerated timeline recently.
sentences.zh: 加速的时间线上。

sentences.en: I mean, the pace of innovation, it truly feels like super speed on a different level.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，创新的步伐，真的感觉像是处于另一个层面的超高速。

sentences.en: Is that wrong?
sentences.zh: 那是错的吗？

sentences.en: Is that just me?
sentences.zh: 还是只有我这么觉得？

sentences.en: I mean, it has.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实如此。

sentences.en: But a lot of stuff that has changed doesn't have industrial impact, right?
sentences.zh: 但很多已经改变的东西并没有产生工业影响，对吧？

sentences.en: Like whenever someone lays off a bunch of people saying we're going to replace them with AI, often they discover if you follow them six months later, they had to rehire a
sentences.zh: 就像每当有人裁掉一大批人说我们要用人工智能取代他们时，如果你在六个月后跟踪他们，通常会发现他们不得不重新雇佣

sentences.en: bunch of them because it just didn't work.
sentences.zh: 其中的一部分人，因为这根本行不通。

sentences.en: So yes, there is a massive acceleration on a cultural level that can often be quite alarming.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，在文化层面上确实存在巨大的加速，这往往会非常令人担忧。

sentences.en: But if you go around and talk to companies, big companies like the ones that are, you know, moving the economy, it hasn't really happened there.
sentences.zh: 但如果你去和公司交流，那些推动经济的大公司，这种情况并没有真正发生。

sentences.en: And you can even see that, of course, in my reporting, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，你甚至可以在我的报道中看到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Small little companies, startups, yeah, they're moving really faSt.
sentences.zh: 小公司，初创公司，是的，它们行动得非常快。

sentences.en: Google, they're moving 10% faster.
sentences.zh: 谷歌，他们快了10%。

sentences.en: And I think that's closer to the impact you might see if you look at white-collar work writ large.
sentences.zh: 我认为这更接近你从广义上观察白领工作时可能看到的冲击。

sentences.en: There is something comforting about that, I have to just admit.
sentences.zh: 我不得不承认，这一点确实让人感到些许安慰。

sentences.en: So we've been talking a lot about the shift in the work of the people who are making software.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直在谈论软件开发人员工作方式的转变。

sentences.en: I want to ask you about what they're actually creating and how the innovation that we've been talking about might change that.
sentences.zh: 我想问你关于他们实际创造的东西，以及我们一直在谈论的创新可能会如何改变这一点。

sentences.en: Like, what is the upshot of all of this for those of us who will mostly interact with it
sentences.zh: 比如，对于我们这些主要通过与这些人制作的产品进行交互来使用它的人来说，这一切的结果是什么？

sentences.en: by interacting with the products that these people make?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这一切对我们其他人有什么好处？

sentences.en: In other words, what is the upside for the rest of us of all of this?
sentences.zh: 我想其中一个好处是，我们似乎生活在一个拥有海量软件的世界里，对吧？

sentences.en: I guess one of the upsides is that it feels like we live in a world where there's tons of software, right?
sentences.zh: 只是20年前不存在的东西。

sentences.en: Just stuff that didn't exist 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 社交网络，你知道，短信。

sentences.en: Social networks, you know, text messaging.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看工作世界，有大量的事情从来没有真正得到过软件的帮助。

sentences.en: But if you look at the world of work, there is just a massive amount of things that have really never been helped out by software at all.
sentences.zh: 我无法告诉你我与多少家公司交谈过。

sentences.en: I can't tell you how many companies I talk to.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是5000万美元规模的混凝土搅拌公司。

sentences.en: They're like $50 million, you know, concrete mixing firm.
sentences.zh: 他们希望能有更好的软件来运营公司。

sentences.en: And they would like to have better software to run their company.
sentences.zh: 但他们什么都没有，因为对于一家5000万美元的公司来说这听起来很奇怪，

sentences.en: And they don't really have anything because it sounds weird for a $50 million company,
sentences.zh: 但他们规模不够大，无法雇佣五名软件人员来制作定制软件。

sentences.en: but they're not big enough to be able to hire like five software people to make custom software.
sentences.zh: 他们负担不起。

sentences.en: They can't afford to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只能在Windows XP电脑上用三个Excel电子表格勉强维持整个公司的运营，

sentences.en: So they just toddle along running their entire company on three Excel spreadsheets on a Windows
sentences.zh: 他们不敢更新系统，因为那会破坏他们用来跟踪所有费用的所有东西。

sentences.en: XP computer that they're afraid to update because that will break everything that they're using to track all their expenses.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，大量这类中型企业在技术方面服务严重不足。

sentences.en: An astonishingly large number of these midsize firms are horribly underserved by technology.
sentences.zh: 如果你在这些公司工作，你就知道那是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And if you work at one of these companies, you know what it's like.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果编写软件变得更容易，如果你能拥有一个世界，比如，好吧，

sentences.en: So if it becomes easier to write software, and if you could have a world where like, okay,
